title: The History of Fallout | From Vault Dwellers to Amazon | Gaming History
description: The full history of Fallout: Interplay's first games, Bethesda's purchase in 2007, Fallout 3, New Vegas, Fallout 4, Fallout 76, the Amazon series and the big announcements from July 2026.

sections.heading: War never changes
sections.script: A Vault Boy with a thumbs up, a wasteland full of surprises and the famous line that war never changes. Fallout is one of the most recognizable role playing series in gaming, with a style all its own: nineteen fifties optimism mixed with a world after nuclear disaster, and a dark sense of humor that makes it unforgettable. In this video we trace the whole history of the series. We start with the original games from Interplay, move to Bethesda's purchase of the series in two thousand seven, and visit Fallout Three, New Vegas, Fallout Four and Fallout Seventy Six. Then we look at the hit Amazon series and the big announcements from this summer. Step out of the vault with us.

sections.heading: Where it all began
sections.script: The story begins in October of nineteen ninety seven, when Fallout: A Post Nuclear Role Playing Game was released for computers by Interplay. It put players in the shoes of a vault dweller sent out to find a replacement part for their home, and it gave them freedom to solve problems by talking, sneaking or fighting. The sequel, Fallout Two, followed in October of nineteen ninety eight and was made by Black Isle Studios. The first two games were loved by role playing fans for their choices and consequences, though they were more a critical success than a big commercial hit. Together they created the foundation for the entire series, from the retro future look to the dark humor.

sections.heading: A new home at Bethesda
sections.script: After the early games, the series entered a quiet period. Interplay was struggling financially, and in two thousand seven Bethesda Softworks bought the Fallout brand from Interplay for five point seven five million dollars, according to reports of the deal. Before that, Bethesda had only held a license to make a Fallout game, while Interplay kept ownership. Bethesda was already famous for The Elder Scrolls, including Morrowind and Oblivion, so fans were curious and nervous at the same time. Could a studio known for big first person open worlds keep the spirit of the classics alive? The answer would come with a big new game just a year later.

sections.heading: Fallout Three
sections.script: Fallout Three, made by Bethesda Game Studios, was released on October twenty eighth, twenty oh eight. It moved the series into a fully three dimensional first person world and set it in the ruins of Washington, D.C., with the Capitol Wasteland full of strange places to explore. The V.A.T.S. system let players pause the action and target body parts in slow motion. The game earned great reviews and brought the series to a much larger audience than the older titles ever had. For many players today, Fallout Three is where their own story with the wasteland started, and it turned a niche role playing series into a global name. If you have ever wandered the wasteland with a dog by your side, chances are this is where the modern Fallout formula first took shape, and many of its ideas are still used today.

sections.heading: New Vegas
sections.script: In October of twenty ten came Fallout: New Vegas, released on October nineteenth in North America. Instead of Bethesda Game Studios, the developer was Obsidian Entertainment, a studio with its own long history in role playing games. Bethesda published it, and the game arrived only two years after Fallout Three. The game moved to the Mojave Desert and was built around factions, reputation and choices that could change the ending in surprising ways. It is not a direct sequel to Fallout Three, and fans praise its writing and its many ways to play. Even after all these years, New Vegas still tops many favorite game lists, and that is why the news about its remaster has excited so many players.

sections.heading: Fallout Four and Fallout Shelter
sections.script: The year twenty fifteen was a big one. In June, Bethesda released Fallout Shelter on iOS, a mobile game in which you run your own vault. It later came to Android, PC and consoles. Then, on November tenth, twenty fifteen, Fallout Four arrived on PC, PlayStation four and Xbox One, from Bethesda Game Studios. Set in Boston, it gave players a voiced hero, a companion dog, and a settlement building system that let them create their own bases. The game was a big success and stayed popular for years, helped by mods and later updates. Between Shelter and Fallout Four, the series reached more people than ever before.

sections.heading: Fallout Seventy Six
sections.script: On November fourteenth, twenty eighteen, Bethesda released Fallout Seventy Six for PC, PlayStation four and Xbox One. It was the first online Fallout, set in West Virginia, where players explore the wasteland together with friends. The launch was rough, and many players were unhappy with the state of the game. But Bethesda kept working on it. Over the following years the game received many updates and expansions, and it slowly turned into a healthy online game with a loyal community. The game also shows how a series can grow in new directions. It is a good reminder that a game's story does not end at launch, and Fallout Seventy Six is still receiving new content today.

sections.heading: Fallout on Amazon
sections.script: In April of twenty twenty four, the Fallout television series arrived on Prime Video, made by Amazon together with Bethesda. Amazon said the first season was watched by sixty five million viewers within its first two weeks. Season two premiered in December of twenty twenty five, set in the Mojave around New Vegas, and Amazon reported more than eighty three million viewers for it in its first thirteen weeks. The series has also been renewed for a third season. Amazon says the franchise has passed one hundred million viewers in total, and the show sent many new players back to the games.

sections.heading: July twenty twenty six: big news
sections.script: Now to the latest. On July seventeenth, twenty twenty six, Bethesda Game Studios published a note about the future of the series. It confirmed that remasters of both Fallout Three and Fallout: New Vegas are in development, though no dates or platforms were announced. It also confirmed that Obsidian is working with Bethesda on a new Fallout game, and that Fallout Five is in pre production. Bethesda called Fallout Five its long range destination, built on Creation Engine Three, the same engine as The Elder Scrolls Six. The Elder Scrolls Six remains the studio's main focus, so patience will be needed.

sections.heading: Thirty years of Fallout
sections.script: There is more to look forward to. In the same note, Bethesda said the next major expansion for Fallout Seventy Six, called Raven Rock, is coming in twenty twenty seven, and that it is a prequel story to Fallout Three. Twenty twenty seven is also the thirtieth anniversary of the series, counting from the first game in nineteen ninety seven, and Bethesda plans to celebrate with a live event in Washington, D.C. There will be no Fallout Day broadcast this year, because the studio is saving the big celebration for next year. So the wasteland is going to get busy very soon.

sections.heading: Which Fallout is your favorite
sections.script: From a vault in nineteen ninety seven to a global series with its own hit television show, Fallout has come a very long way. Now we want to hear from you. Which game is your favorite: the classic Fallout Two, Fallout Three, New Vegas or Fallout Four? Are you more excited about the remasters, the Obsidian game or the thirtieth anniversary? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history, and we will see you out in the wasteland. Stay safe, vault dweller.
